cases.summary: Between 2026-09-29T22:30:00Z and 22:32:00Z, GPU 1 on node a6test-a100-node-02 showed a rising PCIe replay counter (ev-0: 176, ev-1: 331, ev-2: 505 in 10 min), while other GPUs on the node showed pcie_replay_increase=0. Metrics confirm GPU 1 had pcie_replay_increase=3058 (cumulative), power at default 400W (no power capping), normal temperatures (64-67°C), no ECC or NVLink degradation, and throttled samples (76). No BMC or XID log entries were found. Similar past incidents (inc-2025061, inc-2025047, inc-2025019) all resolved with reseating the riser or replacing a PCIe cable; root causes were 'riser not fully seated' or 'degraded PCIe cable'. Thus, the observed steady rise in PCIe replays indicates PCIe link degradation (pcie_degradation), not noisy_neighbor (no error counters rose besides pcie_replay), power_fault (power limit at default), or thermal_runaway (temperatures normal).
cases.rationale: PCIe replay counter rising steadily indicates link degradation; runbook says 'Replays without errors are not urgent, but they often come before a GPU falls off the bus. Schedule a drain.' Reseat the GPU riser or cable during maintenance as per remediation. Drain the node to prevent potential GPU off-bus failure while maintenance is scheduled.

cases.summary: GPUs 4-6 on node a6test-a100-node-03 ran 12-13°C hotter than their power draw predicts (thermal residual), reached 85-86°C, and experienced thermal throttling (SM clocks dropped to ~750-780 MHz vs ~1230 MHz on neighbors). Neighboring GPUs 0-3 remained normal (~63-65°C, ~1230 MHz clocks). No ECC, PCIe replay, or NVLink CRC increases. Power limit at default 400 W (no power cap). Logs empty (no BMC fan error). This matches thermal runaway symptoms: GPU temperatures climb while power stays flat/drops, thermal slowdown appears before throttling, and neighboring GPUs stay cooler. Similar past incident (inc-2025049) resolved by draining and hot-swapping the failed fan.
cases.rationale: Thermal runaway detected with thermal residual >5°C hotter than power, SM clock drop, and throttling. Neighboring GPUs normal. Past similar incident resolved by draining and hot-swapping the failed fan. Drain node to allow inspection and replacement of potentially failed fan module; human approval required for drain.

cases.summary: GPU 5 on node a6test-a100-node-01 fell off the bus (XID 79) at 2026-09-30T05:17:04Z, coinciding with a BMC critical PCIe fatal error on GPU slot 5. Telemetry shows GPU 5 stopped reporting (samples dropped from ~282 to 174, last_minute at 05:16:00Z while neighbours reported at 05:34:00Z), confirming the GPU disappeared from telemetry. No thermal runaway signs (temperatures ~65-67°C, power ~379 W at default 400 W limit), no power cap or ECC/PCIe/NVLink degradation. The evidence matches the gpu_off_bus symptoms: XID 79 error, PCIe fatal error, and missing GPU samples.
cases.rationale: Per the gpu_off_bus runbook remediation: 'Drain the node (rb-009-node-drain). The GPU can't be recovered while the OS is running.' Reboot will be performed after drain.

cases.summary: Between 12:55-13:18 UTC on 2026-09-30, GPU 0 and GPU 1 on node a6test-h100-node-04 showed rising NVLink CRC error counters (nvlink_crc_increase: 4373 for GPU 0, 4155 for GPU 1) and XID 74 error 'NVLINK Error. Link 3 CRC errors' at 13:17:44Z. Temperatures were normal (~63°C), power draw ~577W (default 700W, no power capping), and utilization ~79%. Other GPUs showed no NVLink CRC increases. Throttled samples increased on the affected GPUs (35 and 26), consistent with link degradation slowing jobs. No ECC, PCIe replay, or thermal runaway signs. This matches NVLink degradation symptoms: CRC errors climb on two GPUs sharing a link, XID 74 observed, and multi-GPU slowdown.
cases.rationale: NVLink CRC errors are climbing on GPUs 0 and 1 (link degradation), causing throttling and performance impact. According to the runbook, drain the node to stop jobs from using degraded links while resetting/retraining the links. Drain requires human approval for sev2; after drain, reset GPUs or reboot to retrain links.

cases.summary: Between 2026-09-30T13:34:00Z and 2026-09-30T13:45:24Z, NVLink CRC error counters on GPU 2 and GPU 3 increased rapidly. The node metrics show nvlink_crc_increase of 4201 for GPU 2 and 4106 for GPU 3 (cumulative over the window), with nvlink_crc_errors_total reaching 67-101 in 10 minutes per evidence (ev-0, ev-1, ev-3). At 13:44:24Z, XID 74 'NVLINK Error. Link 3 CRC errors' was logged (ev-23). Temperatures are normal (61.5-67.6°C), power averages are ~340W (below default 400W but not power-capped; power_limit is 400W), and no thermal runaway or throttling beyond normal (throttled_samples 25-39 vs 342 total). No ECC or PCIe replay errors were observed. GPUs 2 and 3 share an NVLink link (adjacent indices), matching the NVLink degradation symptom pattern (CRC counters climb on two GPUs sharing a link, XID 74 error present). Therefore, the root cause is nvlink_degradation.
cases.rationale: NVLink degradation slows every job that uses the affected link (symptoms). The runbook recommends draining the node for NVLink degradation to avoid performance impact while investigating, and resetting GPUs or rebooting to retrain links. Since this is sev2 and errors are present (XID 74), drain the node first; reset GPUs can be attempted after drain if needed.

cases.summary: GPU 6 on node a6test-a100-node-02 showed rising correctable ECC errors (ecc_sbe_total from 5 to 53 in 30 min), retired pages (1 page retired at 23:34, 00:17, 00:45), and culminated in an XID 48 DBE (Double Bit Error) ECC error at 01:35:44Z. Metrics show ecc_sbe_increase=327 and ecc_dbe_increase=1 for GPU 6, while other GPUs show no ecc_dbe_increase and only minor ecc_sbe_increase (0-1). Temperatures were normal (64-67°C), power was at default limit (400 W), and no thermal throttling or power capping was observed. This matches the ECC degradation symptoms: correctable errors rising to dozens per hour, retired pages increasing, and DBE error appearing. No signs of power fault (power limit at 400 W), thermal runaway (temps normal, no thermal residual), noisy neighbor (power limit default, no temp/power rise without error counters), or GPU off bus (GPU still reporting). Thus, the root cause is ecc_degradation.
cases.rationale: Per the ECC degradation runbook, sev1 incidents occur on DBE or XID 95. Acting on the trend allows moving work off the GPU before job crashes. Since a DBE error (XID 48) already occurred at 01:35:44Z, draining the node to move work off GPU 6 is recommended. The node should be drained (human approval required) and the GPU replaced if ECC errors persist.

cases.summary: At 2026-09-30T21:21:14Z, BMC logged 'PSU1 has detected errors of type Input lost' (ev-0). At 21:22:00Z, all 8 GPUs on a6test-h100-node-01 had their enforced power limit reduced from 700 W (nominal H100) to 420 W (ev-1, ev-2, ev-3). Metrics show all GPUs under the 420 W cap: GPU 6 (index 6) had 71% utilization, 57°C average temperature, and 101 throttled samples, indicating thermal pressure under the cap, while neighbors (GPUs 0,1,4,5,7) stayed cooler (~30-36°C). No ECC, PCIe replay, or NVLink CRC counters increased. This matches past incidents where PSU input loss caused power capping (e.g., inc-2025023#report). The node is currently operating under the reduced power limit, which may cause performance issues and thermal stress.
cases.rationale: BMC reported PSU1 input lost and all GPUs were capped at 420 W. GPU 6 showed throttling under the cap. Past incidents show PSU input loss causes power capping; resolution was PDU breaker reset or PSU hot-swap. Drain the node to avoid running under cap while power issue is resolved by datacenter operations.

cases.summary: Between 2026-09-30T21:38:00Z and 21:41:00Z, GPU 6 on node a6test-h100-node-03 showed a steadily increasing PCIe replay counter (376 → 622 → 909 over three minutes), as recorded in evidence ev-0, ev-1, ev-2. Node metrics show GPU 6 at ~32°C, 122W power draw, 6% utilization, default power limit (700W), and no throttling (throttled_samples=0). GPU 7 on the same node is hot (~68-70°C), heavily loaded (96% utilization), and throttled (90 throttled samples), indicating possible PCIe switch contention. No BMC logs were found. The per-GPU summary shows pcie_replay_increase=5163 for GPU 6 (cumulative), while other GPUs show zero pcie_replay_increase. Symptoms match the runbook's pcie_degradation description (PCIe replay counter increases steadily). This indicates PCIe link degradation on GPU 6's link, which often precedes a GPU falling off the bus.
cases.rationale: Runbook states: 'Replays without errors are not urgent, but they often come before a GPU falls off the bus.' Since the PCIe replay counter increased steadily from 376 to 909 over three minutes and severity is sev3, draining the node avoids potential GPU off-bus failure. Reseat GPU 6 and riser/cable during maintenance per remediation guidance.

cases.summary: GPU 3 on node a6test-a100-node-03 showed rising correctable ECC errors (ecc_sbe_total from 5 to 51 in 30 min), one page retired twice (ev-59 at 02:55 and ev-94 at 03:29, ev-113 at 03:47), and finally a DBE (Double Bit Error) uncorrectable ECC error (XID 48) at 04:23:04Z. Metrics show ecc_sbe_increase=278 and ecc_dbe_increase=1 for GPU 3 while all other GPUs on the node show 0 for both increases. Temperatures (avg ~63-66°C) and power (avg ~375-377 W at default 400 W limit) are normal and similar across GPUs, with no thermal runaway or power capping; utilization is consistently high (~92-93%) across GPUs. No PCIe replay or NVLink CRC increases were observed. This matches the ECC degradation symptoms: correctable errors rising to dozens per hour, retired pages increasing, ending in an uncorrectable DBE error (XID 48). The node's other GPUs (including GPU 7 idle at ~30°C) show no signs of thermal or power issues, ruling out noisy_neighbor.
cases.rationale: Per the ECC error degradation runbook, act on the trend to move work off the GPU before a job crashes. Since a DBE (XID 48) uncorrectable ECC error has already occurred (sev1), draining the node prevents job crashes on the faulty GPU and allows hardware inspection/replacement. The node should be drained (human approval required for drain_node).

cases.summary: At 2026-10-01T02:20:04Z, GPU 4 on node a6test-a100-node-01 emitted XID 79 ('GPU has fallen off the bus') and the BMC logged a critical 'PCIe fatal error on GPU slot 4'. At 02:22:00Z, the GPU stopped reporting samples (observed 0 vs threshold 1), confirmed by metrics showing GPU 4 had only 174 samples vs 282 for other GPUs over the window. Temperatures were normal (~65°C), power draw ~383W at default 400W limit (no power cap), and no ECC, PCIe replay, or NVLink CRC degradation counters increased. This matches the GPU fell off the bus symptoms (XID 79 + PCIe fatal error + missing telemetry) and rules out thermal runaway (no temp spike or residual), power_fault (no enforced power limit below default), or noisy_neighbor (no power cap or thermal residual). The root cause is consistent with a PCIe link failure (slot/riser/cable) or GPU power delivery issue.
cases.rationale: Per the runbook 'GPU fell off the bus (XID 79)', step 1 is to drain the node because the GPU cannot be recovered while the OS is running. Reboot after drain is recommended; DCGM diagnostics level 3 should be run after reboot if GPU returns.

cases.summary: GPU 5 on node a6test-h100-node-01 fell off the bus (XID 79 observed at 2026-10-01T10:08:54Z). The GPU stopped reporting telemetry (samples=0 from 10:11:00Z), while neighbors continued reporting. Metrics show GPU 5 at 70.6°C average, 98% utilization, and 105 throttled samples, with neighboring GPUs 6-7 at ~68-69°C and ~96-98% utilization (also throttled). Power limit is at default 700 W (no power cap), and no ECC/PCIe/NVLink error counters increased. The XID 79 error and missing samples directly match the gpu_off_bus symptom; neighbors' similar hot/throttled state rules out thermal_runaway (where only the failing GPU would be hotter while neighbors stay cooler). No BMC PCIe fatal error was logged, but XID 79 alone is sufficient evidence for gpu_off_bus. The runbook indicates a node reboot is required after XID 79.
cases.rationale: Runbook rb-004-gpu-off-bus states: 'Drain the node (rb-009-node-drain). The GPU can't be recovered while the OS is running.' and 'Reboot the node; a GPU reset is not enough after XID 79.' Since severity is sev1 (capacity loss and failed jobs), draining the node before reboot is required. The action targets the node, not a specific GPU.

cases.summary: Between 11:36-11:39 UTC on a6test-a100-node-02, GPUs 0-3 ran 14-15°C hotter than their power draw predicts (thermal residual), reached 83-86°C, and began thermal throttling (multiple throttle reasons: 1-3). GPUs 4-7 remained cooler (~63-65°C) with less throttling. Power limit was at default 400 W (no power capping), and no ECC/PCIe/NVLink error counters increased. No BMC logs were collected. This matches thermal runaway symptoms (thermal residual >5°C, throttling, higher temps on affected GPUs vs neighbours) and past incidents where failed fan modules caused identical patterns.
cases.rationale: Thermal runaway detected on GPUs 0-3 with thermal residual >5°C and throttling; consistent with past failed fan module incidents (inc-2025049, inc-2025063). Draining the node allows safe inspection and hot-swap of the suspected fan module. Severity is sev2, so node should not continue serving jobs.

cases.summary: Between 2026-10-01T11:38:00Z and 2026-10-01T12:03:54Z, NVLink CRC error counters (nvlink_crc_increase) rose to 4460-4487 on GPUs 6 and 7 (indices 6 and 7), while all other GPUs on the node showed nvlink_crc_increase=0. The node metrics show GPU 6 at 566 W avg power (below default 700 W but not power-capped), GPU 7 at 576 W avg power, temperatures normal (62-71°C), and no ECC or PCIe degradation. XID 74 'NVLINK Error. Link 3 CRC errors' was logged at 12:03:54Z. This matches the NVLink degradation symptom where two GPUs sharing a link show rising CRC errors, with no thermal runaway (neighbours cooler), no enforced power limit below default, and no ECC/PCIe errors. The evidence directly supports nvlink_degradation as the root cause.
cases.rationale: According to the NVLink degradation runbook, degraded links slow every job that uses them, and the remediation recommends draining the node (rb-009-node-drain) and resetting GPUs or rebooting to retrain links. Since this is a sev2 incident with NVLink CRC errors on two GPUs sharing a link, draining the node prevents performance impact on jobs using the degraded links while allowing safe reset/retraining afterward.
